units.text: The treaty signing date and location are supported; the price of $10 million is contradicted by multiple sources stating $15 million as the final price or $15 million asking price.

judgement.reason: The date and Paris location are supported, and one Wikipedia passage states $15 million was offered/total, but the passages do not show multiple sources contradicting a $10 million price, since only one source mentions $15 million.

units.text: Initial U.S. authorization was $10 million for New Orleans only, not the full territory price; the final treaty price was $15 million.

citations.title: Louisiana Purchase - The 10 Best and 10 Worst U.S. Foreign Policy Decisions - The 10 Best and 10 Worst U.S. Foreign Policy Decisions

judgement.reason: The passages support the $10 million initial authorization being for less than the full territory and the final $15 million price, but they specify the authorization was for New Orleans and the Floridas, not New Orleans only.

units.text: Sources consistently cite $15 million as the agreed purchase price for the entire Louisiana Territory; no source confirms $10 million as the treaty price.

citations.title: The Louisiana Purchase: Jefferson’s constitutional gamble | Constitution Center

judgement.reason: Passage 3 states the negotiators made a deal for the $15 million purchase of the entire territory, and the only $10 million mention is Monroe's spending authority limit, not the treaty price.
